title: App Permissions
drDigitalIntro:
Apps ask for permissions when they need access to something on your device.
• Common permissions: Camera, Microphone, Location.
• Ask yourself: does this app actually need this?
• A puzzle game asking for your camera is suspicious. A photo-sharing app asking is not.
• You can always say no. You can change permissions later in Settings.

playgroundTask.goal: You evaluated and responded to app permission requests

steps.say: Click on Puzzle Quest to see its details.
Click Install. It asks for Camera access, and a puzzle game has no reason to need that.
Click Don't Allow. That permission makes no sense for a puzzle game.
Good. Now search for 'PhotoFun', a photo-sharing app that genuinely does need your camera.
PhotoFun needs Camera access to take and share photos, which is what it is for. Click Allow.

drDigitalSuccess: You read what each app was asking for before agreeing to it. The question is always the same one: does it actually need that to do its job?
drDigitalHint: Read what each app is asking for. Deny anything that does not make sense for what the app does.
